context.title: Parables of the Kingdom
context.summary: From a boat, Jesus teaches in parables: the sower, the wheat and tares, the mustard seed, the leaven, the hidden treasure, the pearl and the net. Then his hometown, Nazareth, takes offense at him.
context.background: A parable is a story or comparison from daily life that carries a deeper point. Jesus says parables open truth to willing listeners and hide it from those who refuse to hear (vv. 10–17).

customs.note: Probably darnel, a weed that looks almost exactly like wheat while young; pulling it early risked uprooting the wheat.
Among the smallest seeds Galilean farmers sowed, yet it grows into a large shrub where birds can perch.

watchFor: Parables often come in pairs: mustard seed and leaven, treasure and pearl.
Nazareth's question, 'Is not this the carpenter's son?', closes the chapter (v. 55).

people.name: Jesus
people.also: Immanuel, Emmanuel, Messiah, Shiloh, Christ, Jesus Christ, Messias
people.summary: Anointed, the Greek translation of the Hebrew word rendered “Messiah”, the official title of our Lord, occurring five hundred and fourteen times in the New Testament.

people.name: Isaiah
people.summary: The son of Amoz (Isa. 1:1; 2:1), who was apparently a man of humble rank. His wife was called “the prophetess” (8:3), either because she was endowed with the prophetic gift, like Deborah (Judg. 4:4) and Huldah (2 Kings 22:14-20), or simply because she was the wife of “the prophet” (Isa. 38:1).

people.name: Mary
people.summary: The wife of Joseph, the mother of Jesus, called the “Virgin Mary,” though never so designated in Scripture (Matt. 2:11; Acts 1:14). Little is known of her personal history.

people.name: James
people.summary: The son of Alphaeus, or Cleopas, “the brother” or near kinsman or cousin of our Lord (Gal. 1:18, 19), called James “the Less,” or “the Little,” probably because he was of low stature.

people.name: Jude
people.summary: Judas. Among the apostles there were two who bore this name, (1) Judas (Jude 1:1; Matt. 13:55; John 14:22; Acts 1:13), called also Lebbaeus or Thaddaeus (Matt. 10:3; Mark 3:18); and (2) Judas Iscariot (Matt. 10:4; Mark 3:19).

people.name: Simon
people.summary: One of the brothers of our Lord (Matt. 13:55; Mark 6:3).
